item.title: Bryant man sentenced to 30 years in prison for charges involving production of child pornography
item.description: Tyler Dane Wooten, 36, of Bryant, Arkansas, was sentenced to 30 years in federal prison for multiple federal charges involving the exploitation of minors, including the distribution and production of child pornography.

item.title: Gas prices continue to climb, Arkansas prices higher than the national average
item.description: According to the latest AAA report, the national average for gas has climbed 27 cents in just the past week. It's even worse in the Natural State, which saw an increase of 32 cents in the past week.

item.title: Wrightsville honors 21 African American boys killed in 1959 industrial school fire
item.description: The town of Wrightsville gathered at the Wrightsville Unit of the Arkansas Department of Corrections to remember the 21 African American teenage boys who lost their lives in a fire that broke out in what was then called the Negro Boys Industrial School over six decades ago.

item.title: Little Rock family pleads for justice for loved one in 2024 murder case
item.description: A family in Little Rock is still searching for justice nearly two years after their loved one was shot and killed.

item.title: Former Razorback players reflect on legacy of coach Lou Holtz
item.description: Former Arkansas Razorbacks players are remembering legendary football coach Lou Holtz not only for his success on the field, but for the lasting impact he had on their lives decades after they played under him.

item.title: Pine Bluff man accused of killing wife arrested by U.S. Marshals
item.description: Samuel Wimbly was arrested in Little Rock and will face charges of capital murder and possession of a firearm by certain persons for the March 1 shooting death of his wife, Kinyatta Ringo-Wimbly.

item.title: Kristi Noem is out as Homeland Security secretary, Trump says
item.description: President Trump announced Thursday on social media that he is replacing his embattled Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem with Oklahoma Republican Sen. Markwayne Mullin.
